subject: sociology
title: Sociological Perspectives: Postmodernism & Late Modern Critiques
welcome_lead: Big stories collapse; flexibility, choice and identity take centre stage.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology perspectives postmodernism Bauman Foucault late modernity.
final_note: Postmodern theory doubts foundations — but builds new tools.

concepts.def: Foucault — language and power weaving knowledge.
Identity as basis for political claim.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lyotard (1979): knowledge no longer organised around big stories (Marxism, science, religion). Multiple language games. Baudrillard: media saturated, signs detached from referents — hyperreality. Critics call this nihilism; supporters say it democratises knowledge.

Foucault (1975) 'Discipline and Punish': modern power runs through discourse — knowledge claims producing subjects. Panopticon: prisoners watched without knowing when — internalise discipline. Power is everywhere, not just in state.

Bauman: postmodernity is consumerism's age — identity bought and discarded. Giddens: late modernity, not post — institutions intensified, reflexivity radicalised. Ritzer (1993): McDonaldisation — efficiency, calculability, predictability, control — extends rationalisation globally.

mcqs.q: Foucault's metaphor for internalised surveillance is what?
Ritzer's 1993 concept extending rationalisation globally is called what?

numericals.q: In what year did Foucault publish 'Discipline and Punish'?

free_texts.q: Whose concept of 'hyperreality' describes signs detached from referents?
